title: Bug: Sandbox container not stopped after terminal run despite stop_on_terminal=true
description:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-08-21, clean repro):

GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/files restarts the stopped sandbox container of a TERMINAL run and never stops it again.

Mechanism:
- run_files.rs:1201 reconnect_run_sandbox() calls sandbox.activate() unconditionally (line 1220)
- DockerSandbox::activate() -> begin_start() -> docker start on the stopped container
- Nothing ever stops it afterwards (auto_stop=null, worker already exited) -> leaked running container per visited finished run

Repro (3 steps, verified):
1. fabro run context-demo --environment default -> run succeeds, container Exited (stop_on_terminal works)
2. GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/files?scope=committed (dev-token) -> HTTP 200, container state flips to "Up"
3. Server log: "Sandbox start completed" AFTER the run's "Sandbox stop completed"

Also affected (same pattern): handler/sandbox.rs:884 (GET /runs/{id}/sandbox/files), sessions.rs:734. Terminal WS (handler/sandbox.rs:930) activates intentionally.

Historical evidence: containers 01M0GJVW659C / 01M0GG56PQYP were stopped correctly yesterday (FinishedAt, ExitCode 0) and were silently restarted today 08:04/08:05 by web-UI page visits (2 parallel sandbox starts each, matching /files + /sandbox/files in flight).

Fix options (decision needed):
A) Serve terminal-run files from git checkpoint/final_patch instead of activating the sandbox (final_patch fallback already exists; committed scope could come from checkpoint branch store)
B) Ref-counted activation: stop container again after serving when run is terminal AND lifecycle.stop_on_terminal
C) Gate: refuse to activate sandboxes of terminal runs -> degraded response

Note: with container deleted, /files degrades gracefully to source=final_patch (HTTP 200), proving option A/C are viable.

title: Skills: expand_skill parses preamble/context as slash commands; crashes or hijacks stage prompts
description:
## Status

UPSTREAM PR OPEN: fabro-sh/fabro#784 (branch fix/skill-expansion-authentic-input, based on upstream/main 7200d437e to stay conflict-free of #751).

Fix approach: start-only expansion — find_skill_references honors a /command only at the very beginning of the input (after optional leading whitespace); mid-text tokens are context and pass through. Covers both observed failure modes (unknown-token crash incl. the failure_signature echo vector, and the silent prompt-hijack). 3 regression tests reproducing the runs verbatim, 2 legacy mid-line tests updated with in-test rationale; full fabro-agent suite green (638/638); skills.mdx documents the new semantics.

title: Workflow: per-node tool policy attribute (allow/deny tools per agent stage)
description:
## Problem

Workflow agent stages run with NO tool_access_policy: handler/llm/api.rs
(~line 1084) sets permission_level=Full with the comment 'Override
per-stage if a future workflow attribute narrows the scope' — that
attribute does not exist. Every agent node gets the entire tool registry
(shell, write_file, edit_file, subagents, MCP). The only existing
restriction is binary: prompt nodes (shape=tab) get NO tools at all.

## Existing infrastructure

- NamedToolAccessPolicy (fabro-agent/src/session.rs, ToolAccess enum:
  Allowed / RequiresApproval / Denied) + ToolExposureMode
- Already wired for interactive sessions: server/handler/sessions.rs
  build_ask_fabro_tool_access_policy()
- effective_tools() already applies the policy to the tool list

## Proposal

Node attributes, e.g.:
- tools='read' (preset: read_file, grep, glob, list_dir)
- tools.deny='shell,write_file' / tools.allow='...'
parsed in handler/llm/api.rs into a ToolAccessPolicy for the session.
Also expose run-management tools (agent.fabro_tools, currently run-wide
false) per node: run 01M0NJ3QZ1FK53X9DK3BBAN2ED showed the implementer
probing .fabro/ with ls looking for run context it cannot otherwise
reach — a scoped fabro_run_get would replace that guesswork.

## Use cases (from the lab)

- planner restricted to sd + read tools (currently a prompt rule only —
  the model CAN shell out)
- reviewer with read tools but no write/shell (currently forced to the
  tool-less prompt node, which also caps it to a single LLM call)
- implementer without subagent/MCP tools

## Acceptance

- attribute parsed + validated (unknown tool names, preset names)
- enforced in effective_tools() AND the executor (deny actually denies)
- subagent factory inherits the parent policy
- documented in docs/public/agents/tools.md + workflows/stages-and-nodes.mdx

title: Workflow: per-node filesystem scope (glob hide/allow/deny) for agent stages
description:
## Problem

Agents see the full worktree; there is no way to hide files or deny paths
per stage. No hide/exclude/visibility/fs attribute exists anywhere in the
graph/workflow layer (verified by grep). Scope rules are therefore
prompt-only conventions — the model is trusted, not constrained.

## Use cases (from the lab)

- product runs must not touch platform assets (.fabro/, scripts/,
  justfile) — currently a prompt rule (ADR-0002 painpoint channel);
  enforcement would make the rule mechanical
- hide secrets/credentials files from reviewer/planner stages
- implementer limited to product globs (*.go, go.mod, fib_test.go)

## Design constraint: shell is the escape hatch

Tool-layer filtering (read_file/write_file/glob/grep/edit_file/
apply_patch honor the globs) is cheap but bypassable via shell. The
docker sandbox binds NOTHING by design (docker.rs host_config:
binds=None, with an explicit test container_config_has_no_bind_mounts_or_socket)
— the worktree is copied in, so per-node selective materialization is
possible at stage start (stage-scoped worktree view) without mounts.

## Proposal

Node attributes, e.g.:
- fs.hide='.fabro/**,.seeds/**' (read visibility)
- fs.write='*.go,go.mod' (write guardrail; denies writes outside)
Enforcement: (a) builtin file tools honor the globs, (b) if shell is
allowed for the node, document that fs.hide is advisory only — or pair
fs.hide with the per-node tool policy denying shell, (c) optional
stronger mode: selective worktree materialization per stage.

## Acceptance

- attributes parsed + validated (globs compile; conflicting hide/write
  reported by fabro validate)
- builtin read/write tools enforce them; violations return clear errors
- interaction with shell documented
- docs update

title: Workflow: per-node context_updates allowlist + append-only arrays
description:
## Problem

context_updates is a flat last-writer-wins store. Two failure classes:

1. ACCIDENTAL OVERWRITE: any stage can clobber keys another stage owns
   (current_seed_id, review_verdict, implementation_summary...) — nothing
   constrains who may write which key.
2. NO ACCUMULATION: array-shaped information (e.g. the lab's
   workflow_painpoints channel) must be RESTATED IN FULL by every stage
   that appends, because a partial update replaces the list. Miss the
   restatement and earlier entries are lost silently.

## Proposal

Node attributes:
- context.allow_keys=['current_seed_id','current_seed_title','current_seed_brief','workflow_painpoints']
  (allowlist; unset = all keys, for compatibility)
- context.append_keys=['workflow_painpoints']
  (engine merges updates into these keys as arrays instead of replacing)

 fabro validate rule: a stage whose prompt mentions writing a key not in
 its allowlist gets a warning; writes to non-allowlisted keys are dropped
 (with a stage event naming the dropped key).

## Use cases (from the lab)

- planner owns current_seed_* keys; implementer/reviewer must not
  overwrite them
- workflow_painpoints accumulates across stages without restatement
  (ADR-0002 on the lab's meta branch documents the current workaround)

## Acceptance

- attributes parsed + validated
- allowlist enforced on the context-update path (drop + event, not silent)
- append_keys merge implemented with tests (order preserved, per-run)
- docs: context.md gains a 'Ownership and accumulation' section

title: Workflow: preamble value demotion (8KB) makes tool-less reviewers blind; per-node inline budget needed
description:
## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-23): aggregate half absorbed by fabro-a85b

a85b's aggregate demote pass (16KB sum over all preamble values,
largest-first, 1KB floor) is the generalized fix: many sub-8KB values
now demote too. The SPECIFIC tool-less-reviewer blind spot (a single
8.3KB evidence value demoted to a 300-char preview a prompt node can
never open) is NOT solved by the budget — it needs either the evidence
carve-out (a85b design decision 2) or read-tools via fabro-47b5.
Keep THIS seed open for that reviewer-fidelity question; re-scope
after a85b lands and the lab loop is re-measured.

## Bug

artifact.rs demotes any context/preamble value over
PROMPT_INLINE_VALUE_MAX (8KB) to a 300-char preview plus a blob/file
reference. Downstream agents are expected to READ the referenced file —
but a prompt node (shape=tab) has NO tools and can never open it.
Evidence-style command output above 8KB is therefore structurally
invisible to the one node designed to judge it.

## Observed failure

Run 01M0NGQXB67674XQ5YCR1MB4BN: evidence output reached 8.3KB; the
reviewer (prompt node, fidelity=summary:high) received a 4-line preview
and a blob path, rejected twice with 'identical defect', and the loop
could not converge (implementer is barred from fixing the platform-side
evidence script; cancellation required). Painpoint delivered to the
platform mailbox (meta/denkhaus-lab painpoints.jsonl).

## Proposal

One or both:
1. Per-node or graph attribute raising the inline budget for designated
   nodes (e.g. inline_max='16k'), letting workflow authors pay tokens
   for full-fidelity review.
2. A preamble directive that inlines the materialized blob content for
   designated refs (e.g. inline_refs='command.output') regardless of
   size — engine-controlled, no new tool access.

## Acceptance

- attribute parsed + validated (bounds, interplay with artifact
  offloading documented)
- demotion respects it; preamble shows full value
- docs: context.md 'Artifact offloading' gains the attribute and the
  tool-less-reviewer caveat

title: Preamble: compact fidelity omits context_updates — downstream agents re-derive state blind
description:
## STATUS: fixed locally (denkhaus) + UPSTREAM PR #786 OPEN

https://github.com/fabro-sh/fabro/pull/786
(branch fix/current-key-reservation, based on upstream/main, cherry-picked
from denkhaus commit cd0c825e5)

ROOT CAUSE (proven by reproducer): CURRENT_PREFIX was the bare string
'current' — key.starts_with('current') classified ANY user key starting
with 'current' as engine-internal: current_seed_id/current_seed_brief
(our inter-stage contract) were filtered from stage preambles at EVERY
fidelity level and from child->parent propagation. record_result applied
them correctly; the filter dropped them. Explains run
01M0NJ3QZ1FK53X9DK3BBAN2ED fully (blind implementer, 17 wasted calls,
re-claim role violation). The summary:high 'fix' impression was
coincidental (seed found via sd list, not context).

Fix: reservation is exactly 'current_node' (singular) + dotted 'current.*'
(same discipline as graph./internal./thread.). Tests: classification
cases + pipeline-shape regression; context:: 38/38, preamble:: 56/56.

Close when #786 merges upstream AND denkhaus carries the merge. Lab note:
our keys need NO rename — current_seed_id is a natural contract name; the
prefix was the bug. The running server still needs a rebuild from the
denkhaus tree to pick the fix up (binary is on the old nightly).

title: Workflow: post-stage hooks for deterministic painpoint capture (replace LLM relay)
description:
## CORRECTED (research): stage_completed event ALREADY EXISTS

HookEvent enum (fabro-types/src/settings/run.rs:2505 + lifecycle/hook.rs):
RunStart, StageStart, StageComplete, StageFailed, EdgeSelected,
CheckpointSaved, RunComplete, RunFailed. Only the DOCS are incomplete —
run-configuration.mdx documents just stage_start and run_complete.

## Remaining work (this ticket)

1. DOCS: run-configuration.mdx hooks section — document all events,
   payload shape (status, failure_reason, node), blocking semantics
   per event, sandbox/host execution
2. HOOK PAYLOAD: painpoint relay needs the stage's context_updates in
   the StageComplete payload (today: status + failure_reason only) —
   extend payload so a hook can deterministically append declared
   painpoints (the original use case, run 01M0NTS5XCXJ4V88M9MQWKD83G:
   planner CLAIMED file writes it never performed)
3. SYNERGY (upstream vocabulary, a85b corrected): upstream already
   captures responses to stages/{rank:03}-{node}@{visit}/response.md +
   status.json on the metadata branch — StageComplete hooks read those
   standardized records (fabro dump exposes them); materializing them
   into the worktree is a separate low seed

## Original problem (kept for context)

Painpoints flow via LLM restatement (context_updates relay) — lossy by
construction; staged file never existed in run 15 despite prompt
contracts. Deterministic hook appends replace the trust gap.

## FINAL DESIGN (2026-08-23; message-bus alternative evaluated and closed — fabro-meta-8652)

Priority 1 upgrade: PRIMARY platform ticket for cross-stage painpoint
delivery. Code-verified today:
- HookEvent::StageComplete EXISTS (fabro-types settings/run.rs:2510)
- HookContext carries node_id/status/failure_reason but NOT
  context_updates — payload extension is THE enabler (work item 2)
- Hook runs post-stage => engine-added provenance (node_id) free and
  unfalsifiable; no agent restate, no last-writer-wins relay

Flow (replaces the LLM relay completely):
1. Agents keep emitting painpoints in context_updates (emit side unchanged)
2. StageComplete hook receives context_updates, extracts
   workflow_painpoints, appends to .fabro/run-painpoints.jsonl
   DETERMINISTICALLY (sender = hook node_id, not agent claims)
3. Refiner delivers from the FILE (single source of truth); the
   context-key relay + restate paragraphs die (prompts marked interim)
4. Fixes b3aa-class failures structurally: claims never matter

Open technical checks: 8KB demote interaction (workflow_painpoints can
arrive as blob ref in hook input — resolve in the hook path?);
per-node hook config surface in project.toml.

## STAGE 1 SHIPPED (2026-08-23): meta 66ea226ff, lab d0bffefe7

- stage-journal.nu hook live (stage_complete, non-blocking, sandbox,
  [[hooks]] in workflow.toml); schema fabro-journal-v1; visit recovered
  from journal inventory; functional test passed (2 executions ->
  implementer@1/@2)
- refiner REMOVED (graph + script); exit edges direct
- prompts emit context_updates.journal only (restate relay dead)
- .fabro/journal/ ignored in both worlds (runtime data, checkpointed)
- next run verifies: journal files on the run branch after >=1 stage
- work item 2 (HookContext.context_updates) turns data from {} into the
  real payload; work item 3 = docs gap (hooks events) still open

title: CLI: first-class run lifecycle commands (cancel, interrupt, pause, retry) — no more raw curl
description:
## Problem

Run lifecycle control is API-only. The CLI covers lifecycle narrowly and
implicitly:

- CANCEL exists only as Ctrl+C on an ATTACHED run (kill_on_detach=true is
  hardcoded in command.rs when run attaches; attach.rs handle_detach_signal
  calls client.cancel_run). For a run started with --detach (the natural
  pattern for long/autonomous runs), a run started by someone else, or an
  automation-triggered run, there is NO CLI way to cancel — users fall
  back to curl POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/cancel with a bearer token from
  ~/.fabro/auth.json (which is what happened in the denkhaus lab, twice).
- INTERRUPT (/interrupt: forward to worker, abort in-flight LLM), PAUSE,
  RETRY have server routes but no CLI commands at all.
- rm --force deletes active runs (destructive) — not a substitute for a
  graceful cancel.

## Proposal

Add run-control commands with run-ID prefix resolution (like attach):

  fabro cancel  <RUN> [--wait]   # graceful cancel, --wait polls to terminal
  fabro interrupt <RUN>          # API /interrupt (abort in-flight stage)
  fabro pause <RUN> / unpause    # API /pause
  fabro retry <RUN>              # API /retry

cancel maps to the existing client.cancel_run used by the attach path —
same semantics as Ctrl+C, just addressable after the fact.

Suggested alias: a --kill flag on  is NOT needed; the
attach-Ctrl+C path already covers it.

## Acceptance

- fabro cancel works for any non-terminal run the user can see, with
  prefix resolution and clear error for terminal runs
- --wait blocks until terminal state (bounded)
- docs: CLI reference gains the run-control section
- tests mirror handle_detach_signal_with_kill_on_detach_* semantics

title: Agent harness: parallel edit_file calls to the same file silently clobber each other
description:
## Bug

From run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0 review (mulch mx-eba2dd): the
implementer issued parallel edit_file calls targeting ONE file; they
silently clobbered each other — 'lost a strconv import and two run()
call-site updates; caught later by go vet'. Parallel tool execution
(sessions support it) has no same-target write serialization or conflict
detection.

## Why it matters

A silent lost edit is worse than a failed one: the model believes its
edit landed; nothing errors; only a downstream gate or review catches
the drift — if it does.

## Proposal (any or all)

1. Serialize write-tools per file path (mutex keyed on target path)
2. Detect conflicting parallel writes and fail the second with a clear
   'concurrent edit to <path>' error the model can retry sequentially
3. At minimum: apply order-deterministically (by call order, not
   completion race) and log a warning event

## Acceptance

- test: two parallel edit_file calls to one file apply BOTH edits (or
  the second errors visibly), never silently drop
- warning event emitted on same-file parallel writes
- docs: tools.md parallel-execution section states the guarantee

title: Run status: 'succeeded' when the goal is not achieved (seed still open) — boundary state needed
description:
## Problem

Run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0: status succeeded(completed) while seed
fabro-0879 is still in_progress and the goal ('until no open seed
remains') is not met. The graph honestly routes reviewer-failure to
exit with the seed open, but the top-level status misleads automation
and humans alike ('succeeded' implies done).

## Proposal

- A distinct terminal status for 'run ended at a boundary': e.g.
  succeeded_boundary / incomplete (or a conclusion marker
  'N seeds awaiting review')
- The run conclusion should surface the natural next action
  ('re-run to resume review') instead of leaving it inferred

## Acceptance

- run conclusion carries goal-vs-boundary distinction
- API/UI show it; CLI summary prints 'boundary: N seed(s) still open'
- docs: outcomes.md or run-lifecycle doc names the state

title: Preamble: strip trailing routing JSON from rendered responses; dedupe context re-reads
description:
## Problem

Run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0 billed 828k tokens (~$0.40), largely
re-reading duplicated context: the seed brief appears 3-4x per
downstream prompt (planner's full response INCLUDING its trailing
routing JSON, the current_seed_brief context value, and the
implementer's echo in implementation_summary). The routing JSON
duplicates context_updates verbatim.

## Proposal

1. When rendering a stage response into later preambles, strip the
   trailing routing directive (it is data for the engine, not context
   for peers — the parsed context_updates already carry it)
2. Render each context value once (brief in the context table; do not
   also embed it in the response echo)
3. Optional: instruct/allow agents to keep responses terse (done in the
   lab prompts as a stopgap)

## Acceptance

- preamble contains exactly one copy of each context key
- routing JSON absent from rendered peer context
- token accounting on a comparable run drops measurably

title: Skill discovery loads ~36 irrelevant skills into every agent stage (~1.5k tokens)
description:
## Problem

Every agent session in the lab loads ~36 skill descriptions
(scaffold-exercises, shoehorn migration, ...) — ~1.5k tokens per stage,
almost entirely irrelevant to the loop roles. Skills are a repo-wide
concept but stages have narrow needs.

## Proposal

- per-node skill scoping (skills='seeds,mulch' or skills.none), or
- lazy loading (descriptions only on demand — the agent asks for a
  catalog tool), or
- skill groups in .fabro/skills config mapped to node labels

## Acceptance

- a node can run with zero or scoped skill descriptions
- per-stage prompt size drops accordingly
- docs: skills.md gains the scoping section

title: Sandbox: docker provider should auto-build from image.dockerfile (like daytona) with content-hash caching
description:
## Problem

DockerfileSource (image.dockerfile, inline or path) is consumed ONLY by
the daytona provider (snapshot build + dockerfile_sha256 cache key).
The docker provider accepts just image.docker = 'name:tag' — a finished
image. Repos that run docker sandboxes must bake runner images outside
fabro (manual docker build or external CI), or pay per-run toolchain
setup: in the denkhaus lab, mise install costs ~24.5s of every ~32s run
setup (run 01M0NJZGX7BMJAJC3CZJZ0RNT0, events seq 13-14).

## Proposal

docker provider: when image.dockerfile is set (instead of image.docker),
build the image on first use, tag it from the dockerfile content hash
(e.g. fabro-runner-<sha12>), and reuse it while the hash matches — the
same caching discipline daytona applies to snapshots. Runner-image-as-
config then travels with the repo: .fabro/Dockerfile.* + [run.environment]
image.dockerfile path.

## Acceptance

- image.dockerfile works for provider=docker (inline and path forms)
- image is built once per content hash; unchanged dockerfile = no rebuild
- build failures surface as clear preflight/sandbox errors
- docs: environments.mdx docker section documents the field + caching
- a lab-validated example (mise runner) linked in the ticket

title: Workflow: read-only context_read tool (pull access to context values for tool-agents)
description:
## Status: COMPANION of fabro-a85b (preamble delivery: aggregate budget + stage scoping) — build SECOND

Upstream vocabulary (a85b corrected): OFFLOAD (blob store),
DEMOTE (preview+path marker in preamble), BLOB REF / ARTIFACT
POINTER, MATERIALIZE (file into worktree). No 'persistor'/'handles'.

The aggregate demote pass materializes full values as sandbox files
(demote already does this per value) and upstream captures responses
to stages/{rank:03}-{node}@{visit}/response.md on the metadata branch.
context_read gives tool-agents pull access to exactly those files.

Scope unchanged: read-only context tool for agent stages.
- input: context key name OR blob-ref/materialized path
- tool-less prompt nodes unaffected (stage scoping + budget keep
  preambles small; they need no tool)
- validation: read-only enforcement (no write tools)

title: Workflow: per-node preamble scoping (thematic selection instead of chronological fidelity)
description:
## STATUS UPDATE (2026-08-23, vocabulary + design correction)

The DENY-LIST half is realized by fabro-a85b's preamble_stages_ignore
attribute (render-only filter in fidelity.rs; warning-level lint for
nonexistent stage refs — retry_target_exists precedent). Built first,
fork-first, PR as offer.

Remaining HERE (after that lands): preamble_keys allowlist (key-level
thematic selection) and preamble_stages="none"-style coarse modes.
Allow-list semantics invert the default (opt-in vs pass-through) and
deserve their own design round; scaling argument (bigger workflows
leak new stages into every preamble) recorded as the driver.

## Problem

Fidelity levels scale CHRONOLOGICALLY (how much of everything), never
THEMATICALLY (which parts). For role nodes whose working material is
already prepared by a dedicated upstream node, every level is wrong:

Case from the lab (develop loop, run evidence): the reviewer is a
tool-less prompt node. Its entire input need is (a) the seed spec and
(b) the evidence capture — both freshly produced by the deterministic
evidence node in ITS OWN cycle. But fidelity=summary:high (the minimum
that renders command.output) also renders a full '## Stage: <id>'
section per completed stage INCLUDING all LLM responses — in a
review-loop that grows every cycle: planner@1..N, implementer@1..N,
reviewer@1..N responses all re-read. Fidelity=truncate would drop the
evidence entirely (no context values rendered). Context grows
unboundedly with loop iterations while the reviewer's ACTUAL need stays
constant.

## Proposal

Per-node preamble scoping alongside fidelity — thematic selection:

  reviewer [
      ...
      preamble_keys="current_seed_id,current_seed_brief,command.output,review_feedback",
      preamble_stages="none"      # omit stage-history sections
  ]

Semantics:
- preamble_keys: allowlist of context keys rendered (in addition to
  goal/run-id header); '*' = all (default, preserves current behavior)
- preamble_stages: 'all' (default) | 'none' | 'last' (most recent stage
  only)
- orthogonal to fidelity: fidelity still governs detail LEVEL of what is
  selected; scope governs WHAT is selected
- validation: preamble_keys naming keys that cannot exist (typo) warns

## Relation to discussion #785

This is the push-side complement of context_read (fabro-e804): push
exactly the contract keys a role needs; pull the rest on demand.
Together they let role nodes keep constant context while loops iterate.

## Acceptance

- attributes parsed + validated; defaults preserve current rendering
- a scoped node renders goal + selected keys ONLY (no stage sections
  when preamble_stages=none)
- tests: scoped reviewer constant-size preamble across 3 loop cycles
- docs: context.md fidelity section gains scoping

title: Preamble delivery: aggregate demote budget + per-node stage scoping (upstream vocabulary)
description:
## VOCABULARY CORRECTION (2026-08-23): upstream terms only

This seed previously invented 'Persistor'/'handle'/'outcomes/ files'.
Code research showed upstream already names every piece:

- OFFLOAD: persist a value into the content-addressed blob store
  (>100KB context values become blob://sha256/... refs, artifact.rs)
- DEMOTE: replace an inline preamble value with a preview+path marker
  (>8KB per value, PROMPT_INLINE_VALUE_MAX, marker = PromptLargeValue)
- BLOB REF / ARTIFACT POINTER: the references (blob://..., file://...)
- OUTCOME: upstream type (fabro-types/outcome.rs); responses are
  already captured to stages/{rank:03}-{node_id}@{visit}/response.md +
  status.json on the METADATA BRANCH (not materialized in the worktree)
- MATERIALIZE: placing a file into the sandbox worktree (demote does
  this for demoted values)

'Persistor', 'handle', 'handle delivery', 'outcomes/ dir' are retired.

## DESIGN CHANGE (grilled, R1+): NO interface, no strategy trait

The original vision (deterministic persistor writing .fabro/outcomes/)
is replaced by a minimal fix at the EXISTING seam:

Root cause (verified in code): demote_large_values_for_prompt
(lifecycle/fidelity.rs:204, called once before build_preamble) checks
values INDIVIDUALLY against 8KB. Nine ~3KB responses sum to 25.6k with
no trigger. Also summary:high renders sub-8KB LLM responses fully as
blockquotes (preamble.rs:280) — no line cap.

Fix 1 — AGGREGATE BUDGET PASS: after the per-value pass, sum serialized
sizes of all non-hidden values + outcome updates; if over
PREAMBLE_VALUE_BUDGET (16KB default), demote largest-first until under
budget; values <1KB are never demoted by this pass (contract keys,
enums stay inline for free — no keep-inline list needed). Renderer
already renders the demote marker at all 6 sites incl. response
blockquotes; demote materializes full values as sandbox files (pull
access exists). Zero renderer changes.

Fix 2 — PER-NODE STAGE SCOPING (deny-list): attribute
preamble_stages_ignore = "planner,refiner" on a node omits those
stages' history sections from ITS preamble (thematic selection,
e47c-family). Filter applies render-only in fidelity.rs before
build_preamble; context store untouched (routing, response.* keys,
other consumers unaffected). stage_rendered_keys dedup means ignored
stages' context_updates (e.g. seed brief) still render in the Context
section — exactly what a reviewer needs.

Validation: new lint preamble_stages_ignore_targets_exist in
fabro-validate, Severity::Warning (retry_target_exists precedent:
nonexistent node refs warn, run proceeds; runtime filter matches by
node id, a no-op for missing entries).

Allow-list (preamble_stages=...) deliberately NOT in v1: inverts the
default (opt-in vs today's pass-through); documented follow-up.

## FORK-FIRST (agreed)

Do not gate dev pace on maintainer decisions. Develop on
feat/preamble-stage-scoping (denkhaus base), lab verifies, PR upstream
as an offer. Adopt maintainer's approach only if strictly better.

## Acceptance (updated)

- aggregate pass keeps preamble constant-size across >=3 loop cycles
  (lab assertion, many sub-8KB values reproducer)
- preamble_stages_ignore omits named stages' sections; warning (not
  error) on nonexistent entries; fabro validate covers it
- docs: context.mdx + preamble section use upstream vocabulary
- stages/ materialization split out (see new seed) — no longer blocking

## Supersedes/absorbs

- absorbs: aggregate-budget half of fabro-9467
- realizes deny-list half of fabro-e47c
- companions: fabro-e804 (context_read resolves blob refs/materialized
  files), fabro-900e, fabro-47b5 unchanged

## IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (in progress, branch feat/preamble-stage-scoping)

Commit 1 — preamble_stages_ignore:
1. Node attribute parse: follow the fidelity/retry_target accessor
   pattern in fabro-graphviz Node (comma-separated list, trim, dedupe;
   empty entries dropped)
2. Filter in lifecycle/fidelity.rs BEFORE build_preamble: drop ignored
   node ids from completed_nodes (and their outcomes from the map
   passed to the renderer) — render-only, resolved copies only
3. Lint rule fabro-validate/rules/preamble_stages_ignore_targets_exist
   (Severity::Warning, retry_target_exists shape) + tests
4. Docs: context.mdx preamble/fidelity section

Commit 2 — aggregate budget pass:
5. artifact.rs: PREAMBLE_VALUE_BUDGET (16KB) + PREAMBLE_DEMOTE_FLOOR
   (1KB); after per-value pass in demote_large_values_for_prompt,
   sort candidates by serialized size desc, demote until sum <= budget
   (reuse demote_value_for_prompt; skip already-demoted markers)
6. Tests: (a) many ~3KB values -> aggregate demotes, preamble const;
   (b) small contract keys stay inline; (c) single 20KB value still
   demoted per-value (unchanged); (d) exactly-at-budget boundary
7. Docs: outputs.mdx demote section gains the aggregate budget

Then: lab loop verify (>=3 cycles, preamble size stable), PR upstream
as offer (fork-first posture per ADR-0007).

title: Materialize stages/{rank}-{node}@{visit} records into the worktree (agent-readable)
description:
## Split off from fabro-a85b (vocabulary-corrected)

Upstream already persists every stage record — response.md, status.json,
prompt.md, provider_used.json — but on the METADATA BRANCH
(fabro dump / snapshots expose them), NOT as files in the sandbox
worktree. Agents cannot read their own run's history without a dump.

Low priority: demote already materializes demoted values as files, so
after a85b's aggregate pass the pull path exists for oversized values.
This seed covers making the FULL stage records addressable in-worktree
(e.g. under .fabro/stages/ mirroring the metadata layout) so a
follow-up step can read any prior response on demand.

Open question: worktree materialization must stay checkpoint-stable
(git-tracked? excluded?) — revisit when fabro-e804 (context_read)
shapes the read side.

title: Document + decide: preamble_stages_ignore does not apply per parallel-branch target
description:
## Finding (code-verified, 2026-08-23)

preamble_stages_ignore on a PARALLEL-BRANCH TARGET node is silently
ignored. Verified against the fan-out path:

- Branch preambles are PRE-RENDERED by build_parallel_branch_preambles
  in lifecycle/fidelity.rs, from the PARENT parallel node's before_node
  pass, using the parent's scoping (comment in code: 'Branch preambles
  inherit the parent node's stage scoping').
- Branch target nodes never run before_node themselves (known branch
  path: handler/parallel.rs execute_single_attempt, no lifecycle), so a
  preamble_stages_ignore attribute set on the target has no execution
  point where it could apply.
- The attribute WORKS on: the parent parallel node (applies to ALL
  branch preambles), fan-in nodes with prompts (standard prompt path),
  and all sequential nodes.

## Risk

A workflow author sets scoping on a branch target expecting per-branch
filtering; it silently does nothing. The branch preamble renders all
stage history the parent did not filter. No warning, no validation
error.

## Required work

1. DOCS: context.mdx 'Stage scoping (deny-list)' section gains an
   explicit limitation note: attribute placement on parallel branch
   targets is ignored; set it on the parent parallel node to scope all
   branch preambles.
2. VALIDATION: new fabro-validate rule (warning, inert-attribute
   family like parallel_branch_inert_attribute.rs — PRECEDENT EXISTS):
   'preamble_stages_ignore on parallel branch target X is inert; move
   it to the parent parallel node'. That rule file already flags inert
   fidelity on branch targets — extend the family.
3. DECISION (upstream-facing): either accept the limitation as the
   documented contract (parent-scoped inheritance) or implement
   per-branch scoping by honoring the target's attribute inside
   build_parallel_branch_preambles (needs the target node's own
   preamble_stages_ignore read at pre-render time — data is available:
   target_node is resolved there). Fork-first: docs+lint now on our
   branch; upstream PR offer later.

## Evidence

- lifecycle/fidelity.rs: build_parallel_branch_preambles receives
  completed_nodes/node_outcomes from the PARENT's scoped copies only
- handler/parallel.rs: branch path skips lifecycle before_node
- existing inert-attribute precedent:
  fabro-validate/src/rules/parallel_branch_inert_attribute.rs

title: PR publish robustness: dedicated model + reasoning_effort for PR content; deterministic fallback on LLM failure
description:
## Failure (run 01M0QTNF6GWHGPKHSQ2Y2PB8CQ)

Everything green (loop, gate, review approved, seed closed, run branch
pushed) — then the run FAILED with publish_failed: the PR title/body
generator (single structured LLM call, run model glm-5.3) returned no
JSON ('expected value at line 1 column 1'). glm-5.3 without explicitly
disabled reasoning tends to non-JSON output for structured requests;
the PR call sets NO reasoning_effort (GenerateParams field exists,
wired nowhere in pull_request.rs) — provider default applies.

## Root causes (both code-verified)

1. NO PR-specific model config: build_pr_content uses the run model;
   [run.pull_request] has enabled/draft/auto_merge but no model.
2. reasoning_effort not configurable for the publish step (RunModelControls
   has it for NODES; the PR call bypasses node controls).
3. No fallback on LLM HARD failure: fallback_pr_title(goal) exists but
   only triggers on EMPTY generated title — a failed generate_object
   propagates via ? and kills the run (publish_failed), despite a
   perfect deterministic title (seed title / goal) being available.

## Fix (upstream-PR candidate after the preamble package)

1. [run.pull_request] model = 'zai/glm-4.7-flash' (falls back to run
   model) — decouples cheap titling from the working model
2. [run.pull_request] reasoning_effort passthrough to
   GenerateParams.reasoning_effort (e.g. 'off' for glm-4.7-flash)
3. generate_object error -> warn! + fallback_pr_title(goal) + skeleton
   body; hard failure only when even the fallback cannot form
4. Tests: LLM hard-fail -> run still publishes with fallback title;
   configured model+effort reach the adapter

## Evidence

- log: 'Pull request creation failed error=LLM generation failed: No
  object generated: Failed to parse response as JSON'
- pipeline/pull_request.rs:401 (GenerateParams::new without reasoning),
  :408-411 (map_err + ? propagation), :415-419 (fallback only for empty)
- run branch ee9ca7591 was merged manually (8d26 delivered)

title: Improve workflow (automation): scan run branches for journals, cluster findings, propose workflow changes
description:
## Concept (agreed 2026-08-23)

The platform side consumes the product loop's output as a WORKFLOW of
its own — perfect separation: product loop (denkhaus-lab develop) and
platform loop (this) communicate ONLY through git artifacts (run
branches + .fabro/journal/).

## Pipeline

1. SCAN: fetch origin; iterate fabro/run/* branches of the product
   repo; read .fabro/journal/<node>@<visit>.json (schema
   fabro-journal-v1; provenance engine-side)
2. CLUSTER: group journal data by theme/signature (painpoints,
   observations; consumer-defined ontology — the journal itself has
   none)
3. DECIDE: recognized pattern? (threshold, repetition across runs)
4. PROPOSE: workflow change as PR to the product branch — from a
   PLATFORM branch namespace (fabro/improve/<run-id>) so the product
   quality gate (runs must never touch .fabro/workflows/) is not
   violated; merge via human review

## Trigger

Scheduled Runs exist upstream. Sequence: create automation -> start
MANUALLY first -> cron later. No autonomy before the loop is proven:
stage 4 ships as REPORT only (clusters + suggestions as seeds), PR
drafts after quality is demonstrated, auto-merge NOT planned (self-
modification without human net).

## Dependencies

- fabro-176b stage 2 (HookContext.context_updates) so journal data is
  non-empty; stage 1 shipped, next run proves durability on run branches
- product-side gate rule 'run diff must not touch .fabro/workflows'
  (part of the meta-retirement seed)

## Open

- scan window/retention (all run branches? last N days?)
- clustering approach (LLM vs deterministic grouping by node+kind)

title: Retire meta/denkhaus-lab: single product branch + deterministic gates replace the two-world split
description:
## Decision (2026-08-23)

The two-world architecture (ADR-0001..0005) is retired. Replacement
topology:

  denkhaus      platform: engine code + platform docs/seeds/reviewer
                (docs/lab/: rescued ADRs 0001-0008, docs/fabro engine
                snapshot, docs/reviews, .prime reviewer-agent, mailbox
                painpoints.jsonl — rescue staged in index, uncommitted)
  denkhaus-lab  product: gofib + workflow assets (the ONLY source; the
                sync dance dies with meta)
  fabro/run/*   runs with .fabro/journal/ — the new diagnosis world

## Why now

- journal -> checkpoint -> run branch makes delivery intrinsic; the
  refiner (and its meta mailbox) is already removed (run 01M0QTNF6GW)
- ADR-0008's lesson: protection must be DETERMINISTIC, not topological

## Steps

1. RESCUE: commit the staged meta-exclusive content on denkhaus
   (docs/lab/*, .prime, painpoints.jsonl — 24 files, index ready)
2. GATE RULE (before any deletion!): product qualitygate gains 'run
   diff must not touch .fabro/workflows/' — blocks run-merge-backs
   touching assets; platform work happens via platform-namespace PRs
3. MIGRATE open meta seeds (c9f2 tail_lines cap, b3aa planner claims,
   a7c3 bake toolchain) into the denkhaus tracker
4. ADR-0009 'two loops over one artifact boundary' documents the new
   model; ADRs 0001-0005 stay as history (docs/lab/adr/)
5. DELETE meta/denkhaus-lab (local+remote) after rescue+gate verified
6. AGENTS.md/CONTEXT.md on denkhaus-lab: remove the two-world
   vocabulary, describe single-branch + journal model

## Sequencing note

Retire ONLY after the next run proves journal durability on run
branches (gitignore fix ea92af228 postdates run 01M0QTNF6GW).

UI + events: surface image build while sandbox initializes
description:
## Problem
During a cold runner-image build (~90s in the denkhaus lab, fabro-969f validation) the run detail UI shows only the lifecycle status 'Initializing'. A user watching the page for over a minute has no signal that the image is being built — it looks hung or crashed.

The events exist (sandbox.snapshot.creating/pulling with image name, sandbox.git.started, setup.started) but they are invisible where users look: the header shows nothing, the events waterfall has no sandbox rows (phases + stages only), and the events debug list files sandbox.* under the generic 'System' category.

## Proposal
1. lib/sandbox-activity.ts — pure module over EventEnvelope[]:
   - currentSandboxActivity(events): the latest in-flight activity (building/pulling/cloning/setting-up) with image name, for the run header
   - sandboxActivitySpans(events): completed/in-flight intervals for the events waterfall
2. hooks/use-sandbox-activity.ts — purpose-named hook (react-effects-policy): seeds from a desc-tail listRunEvents fetch, updates from the run SSE stream (subscribeToRunEvents onEvent), active only while lifecycle status is 'starting'
3. run-detail/header.tsx — render activity + first-build hint next to the status badge while initializing
4. run-waterfall.tsx — sandbox activity rows (image build/pull, clone, setup) between phases and stages
5. event-debug-helpers.tsx — 'sandbox' category with its own label/tone instead of System

## Acceptance
- While an image builds, the run header shows 'Building image <tag>' plus a first-build hint instead of bare 'Initializing'
- The events waterfall shows the image-build span as its own row during initialization
- sandbox.* events carry a Sandbox category in the events list
- Pulling, cloning, and setup phases get their own labels/rows
- Page opened mid-build still shows the correct activity (tail-event seeding)
- bun run test + typecheck pass

description:

## Bug
lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/sessions.rs:734 (Ask Fabro session build) calls bare sandbox.activate() with no InspectionSandbox guard and no run-status check. Opening an Ask Fabro session on a TERMINAL run starts the stopped sandbox and nothing ever stops it again — same leak class as the fixed inspection endpoints.

Why the guard does not simply apply: Ask Fabro is a long-lived chat session that NEEDS the sandbox while it lives. This is a different lifecycle concept from read-only inspection (short request, stop on exit):

- read-only inspection: request-scoped, guard restores stopped state on exit
- session-held sandbox: the session OWNS the liveness; sandbox stops when the session ends/expires

## Proposal (decision part of this seed)
Design a session-held-sandbox lifecycle: track that the session activated the sandbox, stop it when the session ends or expires. Consider the degraded alternative for terminal runs (agent runs, sandbox tools answer with a clear error) as the fallback if session-scoped liveness proves too heavy.

## Acceptance
- Ask Fabro session on a terminal run does not leak a running container after session end/expiry
- test covering the terminal-run session path
- vocabulary: keep 'read-only inspection' vs 'session-held sandbox' distinct in code comments

title: hooks: carry stage context_updates in HookContext (journal bridge, work item 2)
description:
## Failure

Run 01M0SS23MJ: every agent emitted journal painpoints via
`context_updates.journal` (engine events prove it — 14 mentions, the
reviewer's blob-ref painpoint reached the planner), but all 12 journal
files on the run branch carry `"data": {}`. The stage-journal hook
writes envelopes without agent payloads.

## Root cause

`HookContext` (lib/components/fabro-hooks/src/types.rs) has no field
for the completed stage's context_updates. The hook reads
FABRO_HOOK_CONTEXT and cannot see what the stage declared. The hook
header itself documents this: 'bridgeless: until HookContext carries
context_updates — engine work item 2'.

## Fix

1. Add `context_updates` (the merged/declared updates map of the
   completed stage) to HookContext, populated for stage_complete.
2. Keep it JSON-typed and Option-al; skip when absent (older callers).
3. stage-journal.nu (meta world, synced) then writes
   `data: ctx.context_updates?.journal?` instead of a hardcoded {}.
4. Tests: a stage with journal context_updates fires the hook with the
   payload visible in FABRO_HOOK_CONTEXT; a stage without updates keeps
   the field absent or empty.

## Evidence

- .fabro/journal/*.json on origin/fabro/run/01M0SS23MJM8972CBJD0SP7T4Q: all data:{}
- events: stage.completed properties carry context_updates.journal.painpoints
- lib/components/fabro-hooks/src/types.rs:11 HookContext — no updates field

title: server: preflight GitHub credential probe + separate publish outcome
description:
## Failure (runs 01M0SS23MJ, 01M0T2GW, 01M0T9B7T6)

Three consecutive runs ended failed(publish_failed) on a 403 from PR
creation — AFTER the graph finished green (seeds closed, gate green,
review approved, run branch pushed). The token authenticates git push
(token_provenance: static, e.g. 01M0T9B7T6 seq 82) but lacks REST-API
scope for PRs. Preflight said 'GitHub Token (minted): contents write,
pull_requests write' — the mismatch is invisible until the last second.

## Fix

1. Preflight credential probe: when pull_request.enabled, validate the
   token against the GitHub REST API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}) during
   fabro preflight AND run submission. One API call; a scope mismatch
   refuses the run in 1s instead of failing after ~8 min and ~$0.35 of
   agent work. Surface which scope is missing in the remediation hint.
2. Outcome taxonomy: publish failure after a green graph is
   succeeded_with_publish_failure (work done, publish blocked), not
   failed. failed implies the dev loop broke — it did not. Keep the
   publish error details + seq + remediation ('branch fabro/run/<id> is
   pushed; fix credentials or open the PR manually') on the run.
3. Retry classification for PR creation: 5xx/timeout -> short backoff
   retry (2 attempts); 4xx -> fail fast with the scope hint. (Run
   01M0T9B7T6: one attempt, failed 16:31:43, run.failed 16:31:45.)

## Acceptance

- preflight fails fast on a push-capable/PR-incapable token with a
  named-scope remediation
- green-graph + publish-failure run reports succeeded_with_publish_failure
- CLI/UI render the two-part outcome (work green, publish blocked + hint)
- tests for probe, taxonomy, and retry classification

## Evidence

- events: pull_request.failed 'Authentication failed creating pull
  request (403)' seq 329, run.failed seq 332 (01M0T9B7T6)
- ADR-0009 (meta/denkhaus-lab): decision context

title: engine: deterministic per-seed cycle counter as context key
description:
## Failure mode

The develop workflow's 3-strikes cycle guard relies on the planner LLM
counting review/gate cycles from preamble history (run 01M0T9B7T6
review, recommendation 1b). A hallucinated count blocks a seed too
early or lets it loop past budget. The engine already tracks
node_visits deterministically; the planner just cannot see it per seed.

## Fix

Deterministic cycle counts injected as a context key, anchored on the
context key that carries seed identity:

- graph attribute (optional), e.g. cycle_counter_reset_key =
  "current_seed_id" — the context key whose VALUE change marks a new
  seed cycle context (engine stays seed-agnostic; the workflow names
  its own key).
- On each stage completion, if the completed node's context_updates
  contain the reset key with a value DIFFERENT from the tracked one,
  snapshot the per-node visit counts as the new baseline.
- Inject internal.seed_cycles = { node -> visits_since_baseline } so
  agents read deterministic counts (reviewer visits since this seed
  was claimed, tester bounces since, ...).
- The develop planner prompt (meta, follow-up) then replaces LLM
  counting with: 'blocked when internal.seed_cycles.reviewer >= 3'.

## Acceptance

- attribute unset -> behavior identical to today (no key injected)
- seed claimed mid-run -> counter starts at 0 for all nodes
- reviewer/tester revisits increment only the matching node counts
- new seed claim resets the baseline
- context key visible in stage preambles; unit tests cover baseline
  reset, increments, and the unset-attribute no-op

## Evidence

- recommendation 1b, run 01M0T9B7T6 review
- ExecutionState.node_visits exists (fabro-core state.rs); Context has
  interior mutability (fidelity lifecycle writes CURRENT_PREAMBLE)

title: engine: dedupe response payloads from context_updates + distinct terminal nodes
description:
## Failure (first auto-merge run review, rec 2a + 1d)

The seed brief appeared FOUR times per checkpoint: as
current_seed_brief, inside response.planner prose, again inside
response.planner's embedded JSON, plus checkpoint context copies. The
12 KB preamble budget blob-ref'd a 1.5 KB brief + 2.0 KB
implementation_summary — budget consumed by COPIES, not information.
And all soft exits (Capture failed, Blocked, Planner/Reviewer failed,
Tracker empty) route to ONE exit node, so run.completed/run.failed
notification routing cannot distinguish success, deadlock-for-human,
and infrastructure failure.

## Fix

1. response.* dedup: when a stage's context_updates carry the same
   data the response text embeds (the JSON contract), stop persisting
   the full response text — or persist the parsed JSON payload only.
   At minimum: exclude context_updates keys that already exist as
   top-level keys from the response echo.
2. Distinct terminal nodes (or exit attributes): success /
   deadlock-for-human (Blocked) / infrastructure failure (capture,
   planner, reviewer) / natural completion (Tracker empty) so
   notification routes and the UI can distinguish them. Exit
   attributes are the smaller change if node identity must stay.
3. Tests: checkpoint context contains each fact exactly once (within a
   tolerance for goal/graph keys); terminal classification maps each
   exit path.

## Acceptance

- checkpoint context: no key duplicates its own response.* payload
- run terminal state exposes exit kind; Slack routes can select on it
- existing workflows unchanged in behavior

title: engine: cycle guards + verification-bounded loops as edge conditions
description:
## Failure mode (review rec 1b follow-up + 4c)

seed_cycles is injected deterministically (fabro-45d0, landed), but the
>= 3 blocking decision still lives in the planner PROMPT —
prompt-resident invariants keep failing silently when edges don't
match (run 01M0SS23MJ: the guard could not fire because no edge
matched). The same applies to the 'at most once per seed' bound on
Verification blocked re-capture: prompt-enforced only, so the loop is
not PROVABLY terminating.

## Fix

1. Edge conditions on context values already parse (condition.rs
   supports context.<key>=<value> and bare keys); add numeric
   comparison for dotted object paths so edges can express:
   condition="seed_cycles.reviewer >= 3" routing planner -> exit
   (Blocked) BEFORE the LLM is consulted, and a structural
   reviewer-loop bound (e.g. seed_cycles.evidence >= 2 forces a
   decide-or-exit edge) so verification re-capture cannot loop.
2. Keep prompt guards as fallback; structural edges win when both
   exist. Document precedence in the workflow docs.
3. The develop workflow (meta, follow-up) then moves its guards into
   graph edges and drops the prompt-side counting entirely.

## Acceptance

- condition parser: dotted path + numeric >=/<= on context objects
- a cyclic test graph terminates via structural guard, not model
  compliance
- unchanged behavior for graphs without guards

title: engine: shared prompt-cache prefix across stages (cache_write_tokens=0)
description:
## Failure (review rec 4e)

Every stage shows cache_read within itself (planner accumulated 41.5k)
but cache_write_tokens=0 EVERYWHERE — each new stage's first call
re-pays the ~4-5k system+tools+skills prefix at full price (~25k
redundant input tokens across five agent sessions in one run).

## Fix

Stable shared system prefix across stages of a run so providers can
cache-write it: identical ordering of system prompt / tools / skills
blocks per role-visit, cache-control headers (or provider equivalent)
on the prefix. Investigate why the current client never sends
cache-write markers (usage shows reads work, writes never happen).

## Acceptance

- cache_write_tokens > 0 on second+ stage of a multi-stage run
- prefix bytes identical across stages for unchanged config
- no behavior change for providers without prompt caching
